title: Construction part
statement: For schemes U,V, v : V ⟶ U and a type E, there exists a morphism satisfying the canonical-section equations and which is an isomorphism.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 18.43 (Tag 093I, sites-modules-section-constant) and Lemma 093R (sites-modules-lemma-pullback-locally-constant), whose omitted proof is this identification; with Sites, Example 0H7J (sites-example-constant-sheaf), the universal property of the constant sheaf, and the adjunction $v^{-1}\dashv v_*$

proof.text: The identity étale object U/U is terminal: the unique map from W/U has underlying morphism W.hom. Base change preserves this terminal object by its finite-limit-preservation instance.

Compose constantSheafAdj at U/U with the continuous-functor inverse-image adjunction. The pushforward followed by sections at U/U is naturally isomorphic to sections at its base change, by the definition of continuous pushforward. Transport the composite adjunction along this natural isomorphism. Its right adjoint now equals that of constantSheafAdj on V at the base-changed terminal object.

Apply Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq to these two adjunctions and evaluate its isomorphism on ULift E. The identity-right-adjoint case of the conjugate-isomorphism unit equation is Mathlib Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. Evaluate this equation at ULift.up e. Unfolding the constant-sheaf unit and composite adjunction unit identifies its two sides with exactly the canonical-section equation in etaleSetInverseImageConstantSheafCondition.
